paper_metadata.title: Epilepsy Surgery for Children With Low-Grade Epilepsy-Associated Tumors: Factors Associated With Seizure Recurrence and Cognitive Function

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting (tertiary pediatric hospital), and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria. While it is a retrospective single-center study, the baseline characteristics are well-documented, and the sample appears representative of pediatric patients undergoing epilepsy surgery for LEATs.

items.reasoning: The authors define the age, clinical condition (epilepsy), and pathological diagnosis (LEATs) clearly.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study requires a 24-month follow-up for inclusion, which inherently limits attrition bias for the primary outcome. However, there is significant missing data for the secondary outcome (postoperative FSIQ), with only 77.8% of the eligible sample analyzed, and no comparison between those with and without follow-up cognitive testing.

items.reasoning: While seizure outcome was available for 100% of the included cohort (due to inclusion criteria), cognitive follow-up was missing for over 20% of the sample.
